units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 27:26">Targ. Y. Deut. XXVII, 26</cite> <he>ברכתא בכ׳ וכ׳</he> blessings in general &c. (v.
<cite ref="Shabbat 147a:8">Sabb. 147ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>נקוט האי כ׳ בידך</he> take this as a rule.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 103b:10">B. Mets. 103ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>כ׳ דמילתא</he> the general rule is &c.

<cite ref="Chullin 95a:12">Ḥull. 95ᵃ</cite> <he>הא דרב לא בפירוש איתמר אלא מכ׳ איתמר</he> this opinion of Rab has not been delivered explicitly but only arrived at by implication; <cite ref="Berakhot 9a">Ber. 9ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Yevamot 21b:10">Yeb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>וכ׳ הוא</he> is this rule without exceptions?—

<cite ref="Shevuot 26a:9">Shebu. 26ᵃ</cite> <he>אהני כ׳ לאתויי וכ׳</he> the generalization (after specification) has the effect of including &c.; a. v. fr.—Pl. <he>כְּלָלִין</he>, <he>כְּלָלַיָא</he>, <cite ref="K00673"><he>כְּלָלֵי</he></cite>. Y. Ter. I, 40ᶜ <cite ref="L00533"><he>לית</he></cite> (<he>כללי׳</he>) <he>כְּלָלוֹי דרבי כ׳</he> the general rules of Rabbi (in the Mishnah; expressions like <he>זה הכלל</he> or <cite ref="E00513"><he>הכל</he></cite>, <he>כל</he> &c.) are not without exceptions.
<cite ref="Ketubot 60a:2">Keth. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>לא … להני כ׳ דכייל וכ׳</he> do not heed those rules which my brother … laid down.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33:3">Gen. R. s. 33</cite> [read:] <he>אליף … כל כ׳ דאורייתא ואילין אינון הלכתא דבבלאי</he> (v. ‘Rashi’ a. l.) he taught Rab … all the general rules (of interpretation) of the Law, and these became the guiding laws of the Babylonians.
